about.title: Monterey Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: A defective product can turn an ordinary afternoon on Del Monte Avenue or Lighthouse Avenue into a trip to the emergency room. Monterey households buy everything from household appliances to bicycles, tools, and vehicle parts, and when one of those items fails because of a flaw in its design, manufacturing, or missing warning, California's strict liability rules generally allow an injured person to pursue the manufacturer, distributor, or retailer without having to prove anyone acted carelessly. That's a meaningful difference from typical negligence cases. If a defective product hurt you or someone in your family in Monterey County, keeping the item exactly as it was at the time of the injury matters — it may be the clearest evidence of what went wrong. LawProactive doesn't practice law; we simply connect you, at no cost, with an independent attorney in our network who reviews product liability matters and works on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless money is recovered.

Lacerations from broken glass or sharp component failure

Traumatic brain injury from failed safety gear or helmets
Amputation or finger injuries from tool malfunctions

whyChoose.title: Why Monterey Residents Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Strict Liability Can Simplify Your Path
items.desc: Because California often applies strict liability to defective products, you may not need to show the manufacturer was careless — just that a defect existed and caused harm.

items.title: Multiple Parties May Share Responsibility
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and retailers can each potentially be held liable, giving an attorney more avenues to pursue on your behalf.

items.title: Evidence Preservation Matters Early
items.desc: Keeping the defective product intact can be critical to proving a design, manufacturing, or warning defect, and an attorney can advise you on safeguarding it right away.

items.question: Do I have to prove the manufacturer was negligent?
items.answer: Not necessarily. California's strict liability framework generally focuses on whether the product itself was defective and whether that defect caused your injury. This is often a lower bar than proving carelessness, though every case depends on its own facts.

items.question: What should I do with the product that hurt me?
items.answer: Try to preserve it exactly as it was at the time of the injury, including packaging, instructions, or remaining parts. This evidence is often central to a Monterey product liability claim, and an attorney can guide you on proper storage and documentation.

items.question: Is there a cost to speak with an attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service connecting injured people in Monterey with independent attorneys, and those attorneys typically work on contingency, meaning they only get paid if you recover money.
